verdicts.reason: A: the logo is pushed to the top-right while the shoe, headline, subline and CTA all sit on the centre axis, so the brand mark looks stranded, and there is a dead band under the CTA. B puts everything on one centre axis (logo, headline, subline, shoe, CTA), which is more coherent. In both, the 'Run lighter' headline is undersized for a 768 square, and B leaves a large gap between the subline and the shoe.

A stacks the shoe, headline, subline and CTA cleanly on the centre axis; its only real flaw is the logo floating off-axis at top-right. In B the left edges don't line up: the logo (x≈100), the headline and subline (x≈246) and the CTA (x≈104) start at three different points, so the text block reads as arbitrarily placed and the right side below the shoe is empty.

A scatters its pieces: the logo is at x≈88 but the headline and subline are indented to x≈178, and the CTA is pushed to the far right on a baseline that matches neither text line. That breaks grouping and reading order, and the headline is weak next to the oversized shoe. B is an orderly centred stack whose only flaws are the off-axis top-right logo and the undersized headline.
